Discreet

dis-KREET -- not to be confused with the similarly pronounced but differently spelled 'discrete' (meaning 'separate'); this unit teaches only 'discreet,' the cautious/tactful sense. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Discreet is careful and cautious in one's speech or actions, especially to avoid embarrassment or attract unwanted attention.

The assistant was known for being extremely discreet about her boss's schedule and personal matters.

Worked Example

A hotel concierge who overhears a celebrity's private conversation never mentions it to anyone, not even to close coworkers, and never brings it up again.

That careful, tactful silence about something sensitive is exactly what discreet means. Unlike 'secretive,' which can sound suspicious, discreet has a respectful, considerate tone.

How Discreet Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tactful

tactful: careful not to cause offense; sensitive

circumspect

circumspect: wary and careful about one's actions

guarded

guarded: cautious about what one reveals

Antonyms

indiscreet

indiscreet: revealing private matters carelessly

blatant

blatant: done openly and unashamedly

How Strong Is It? — tactful → discreet → circumspect

tactful vs. discreet

tactful vs. discreet: Tactful is a bit more general than discreet -- tactful describes being sensitive in how you say something, while discreet more specifically means being careful about what you reveal at all.

circumspect vs. discreet

circumspect vs. discreet: Circumspect can feel more watchful than discreet: discreet mainly describes careful, quiet behavior, while circumspect implies actively scanning a situation for risk before acting.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — dis-

prefix — dis-: apart (Latin)

root — -cret-

root — -cret-: to separate, to sift (Latin (cernere))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin cernere meant 'to separate, to sift, to distinguish.' A discreet person, at its root, carefully sifts and separates what should be said from what shouldn't -- exercising judgment about what to reveal.

Use the root in a new word: discern

Use the root in a new word: discern: It took her years of practice to discern the subtle difference between the two rare wines.
